        <li>
          <p>The Roads API snaps GPS points to the nearest roads, supporting up to 100 points per request and offering optional path interpolation.</p>

        </li>
      
        <li>
          <p>Requests are made via HTTPS using a specified URL with required <code>path</code> and optional <code>interpolate</code> parameters.</p>

        </li>
      
        <li>
          <p>Responses are in JSON format, providing snapped point locations, place IDs, and potential warnings.</p>

        </li>
      
        <li>
          <p>An interactive map demo is available for users to visualize and experiment with the API's functionality.</p>

        </li>
      
        <li>
          <p>Optimal snapping requires input points to be relatively close together, ideally within a few city blocks.</p>

        </li>

<p>The <span class="notranslate">Roads API</span> takes up to 100 GPS points
collected along a route, and returns a similar set of data, with the points
snapped to the most likely roads the vehicle was traveling along. Optionally,
you can request that the points be interpolated, resulting in a path that
smoothly follows the geometry of the road.</p>

<h2 id="requests" data-text="Requests" tabindex="-1" role="presentation"><span class="devsite-heading" role="heading" aria-level="2">Requests</span><button type="button" class="devsite-heading-link button-flat material-icons" aria-label="Copy link to this section: Requests" data-title="Copy link to this section: Requests" data-id="requests"></button></h2>

<p>You must send requests to snap to road using HTTPS in the following form:</p>

  </p><div data-code-snippet="true" data-github-path="third_party/devsite/developers/en/maps/_openapi-specification/dist/documentation/parameters/maps_http_parameters_snaptoroads.html" data-git-revision="main" class="prettyprint notranslate lang-json"><h2 id="required-parameters" data-text="Required parameters" tabindex="-1" role="presentation"><span class="devsite-heading" role="heading" aria-level="2">Required parameters</span><button type="button" class="devsite-heading-link button-flat material-icons" aria-label="Copy link to this section: Required parameters" data-title="Copy link to this section: Required parameters" data-id="required-parameters"></button></h2><ul><li><h3 class="parameter-name" id="path" data-text="path" tabindex="-1" role="presentation"><span class="devsite-heading" role="heading" aria-level="3">path</span><button type="button" class="devsite-heading-link button-flat material-icons" aria-label="Copy link to this section: path" data-title="Copy link to this section: path" data-id="path"></button></h3><p>
      The path to be snapped. The path parameter accepts a list of
      latitude/longitude pairs. Latitude and longitude values should be
      separated by commas. Coordinates should be separated by the pipe
      character: "|". For example:
      <code translate="no" dir="ltr">path=60.170880,24.942795|60.170879,24.942796|60.170877,24.942796</code>.
    </p><div class="note">
      Note: The snapping algorithm works best for points that are not too far
      apart. If you observe odd snapping behavior, try creating paths that have
      points closer together. To ensure the best snap-to-road quality, you
      should aim to provide paths on which consecutive pairs of points are
      within 300m of each other. This will also help in handling any isolated,
      long jumps between consecutive points caused by GPS signal loss, or noise.
    </div></li></ul><h2 id="optional-parameters" data-text="Optional parameters" tabindex="-1" role="presentation"><span class="devsite-heading" role="heading" aria-level="2">Optional parameters</span><button type="button" class="devsite-heading-link button-flat material-icons" aria-label="Copy link to this section: Optional parameters" data-title="Copy link to this section: Optional parameters" data-id="optional-parameters"></button></h2><ul><li><h3 class="parameter-name" id="interpolate" data-text="interpolate" tabindex="-1">interpolate</h3><p>
      Whether to interpolate a path to include all points forming the full
      road-geometry. When true, additional interpolated points will also be
      returned, resulting in a path that smoothly follows the geometry of the
      road, even around corners and through tunnels. Interpolated paths will
      most likely contain more points than the original path. Defaults to
      <code translate="no" dir="ltr">false</code>.
    </p></li></ul></div><p></p>

<h2 id="examples" data-text="Examples" tabindex="-1">Examples</h2>

<p>The following request snaps the specified points to the road geometry. This
particular set of data follows a circular road; setting <code translate="no" dir="ltr">interpolate=true</code>
makes the returned geometry match the curvature of the road. With
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">interpolate=false</code>, the snapped path still follows the road, but the
resulting polyline isn't as smooth.</p>

<ol>
  <li>Click around on the map to create a vehicle track. Note that if your
      points are too far apart, they may not snap correctly.</li>

<aside class="note">Note: The snapping algorithm works best for points that are
  close together. If you observe odd snapping behavior, try creating paths that
  have points closer together. For example, in a city, points should be within
  a few city blocks of one another to improve snap-to-road quality.</aside>
